messages.subject: Re: Getting error "incorrect number of probabilities" in the estimation of M2 statistic.
parts:
I suspected bugs in imputeMissing() would come up sometime since it's fairly new and relatively underused (that is, up until now ;-) ). A part of the function was off for detecting the proper categories to draw (it thought there were more categories than there should be, and occurred when a missing category level was present. i.e., 1,2,3,4,6,7), and has been patched. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Getting error "incorrect number of probabilities" in the estimation of M2 statistic.
parts:
Thanks, Phil! :)

I have a one more question.
May I get about information 'impute' argument in M2()? I still want to know why 'impute = 10' in examples. 10 imputes is enough to calculate M2 with missing data?

2014년 7월 15일 화요일 오전 3시 13분 13초 UTC+9, Phil Chalmers 님의 말:

I suspected bugs in imputeMissing() would come up sometime since it's fairly new and relatively underused (that is, up until now ;-) ). A part of the function was off for detecting the proper categories to draw (it thought there were more categories than there should be, and occurred when a missing category level was present. i.e., 1,2,3,4,6,7), and has been patched. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Getting error "incorrect number of probabilities" in the estimation of M2 statistic.
parts:
The impute options are used to obtain plausible values of what the missing data would look like given a θ input, and the variability is collected using traditional multiple imputation methods. We do this so that we have full datasets to work with, even though they are only instantaneous stand-ins.

So, the number of draws required should be somewhat proportional to the amount of missingness observed. In the examples, 10 was used as just an example, but probably more than 100 or more should be used if missingness occurs a lot. That way variability of the missingness will be better captured in the statistics.
